taskDescription: Arrange this simplified scenario, in which DNA damage first causes cell-cycle arrest and repair fails, in order.
paragraphs: DNA damage activates the sensor kinases ATM and ATR.
ATM and ATR phosphorylate p53, so it escapes ubiquitination by MDM2 and is not sent to the proteasome.
Stabilised p53 accumulates in the nucleus and activates its target genes.
p53 induces p21, which inhibits cyclin-CDK complexes and arrests the cell cycle at the G1/S checkpoint for repair.
If the damage cannot be repaired, p53 induces the pro-apoptotic protein BAX, which releases cytochrome c from mitochondria.
Cytochrome c activates caspases, which dismantle the cell in an orderly apoptotic death.

overallFeedback.feedback: In this scenario, p53 supports arrest and repair: DNA damage detection → ATM/ATR phosphorylation → escape from MDM2-mediated degradation → nuclear accumulation → p21-mediated G1/S arrest, and apoptosis follows only when the damage cannot be repaired. Arrest is not an obligatory precursor to every p53-mediated apoptotic response — p53's response is context-dependent — but loss of p53 removes both the brake and the self-destruct programme.
